content.value_statement: Competitive ad research can be slow and inconsistent. This skill extracts ad examples and turns messaging, creative patterns, and campaign themes into clear insights.
actual_capabilities: Guides competitor ad extraction from public ad libraries.
Organizes screenshots and saved ad references for review.
Analyzes pain points, use cases, value propositions, and calls to action.
Compares themes across several competitors or advertising platforms.
Produces reports, spreadsheet-ready summaries, decks, or pattern libraries.
limitations: Requires access to the relevant public ad library or search page.
Does not bypass logins, paywalls, rate limits, or platform controls.
Performance conclusions are directional unless engagement data is available.
Users must create original ads and respect intellectual property rights.

use_cases.title: Plan New Ad Tests
use_cases.description: Collect competitor examples and identify messaging angles for new campaign experiments.

use_cases.title: Map Market Positioning
use_cases.description: Compare how several brands describe problems, audiences, and product benefits.

use_cases.title: Build a Creative Reference Library
use_cases.description: Save screenshots, themes, and format notes for future creative planning.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Competitor Extraction
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract current ads from [Competitor] in [Ad Library]. Save screenshots and summarize the main messages, offers, and calls to action.

prompt_templates.title: Messaging Theme Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Focus on one customer problem or product category.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [Competitor] ads about [Problem]. Group the pain points, value propositions, proof points, and creative formats they use.

prompt_templates.title: Competitive Set Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract ads from [Company A], [Company B], and [Company C]. Compare their audiences, messages, formats, and gaps we could test.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Trend Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [Competitor] ads from [Period 1] and [Period 2]. Identify changed themes, new formats, repeated claims, and recommended tests.

output_examples.input: Analyze active Facebook ads from a project management competitor.
output_examples.output: A report with ad count, recurring pain points, top headlines, creative patterns, audience signals, and campaign test recommendations.

output_examples.input: Compare LinkedIn ads from three B2B software companies.
output_examples.output: A side-by-side summary of positioning, offers, proof points, calls to action, and whitespace for differentiated messaging.

output_examples.input: Review video and static ads from one competitor.
output_examples.output: A format analysis that highlights visual patterns, message length, product screenshot usage, and reusable creative hypotheses.

best_practices: Use public sources and respect platform terms and access limits.
Look for repeated patterns before turning observations into campaign ideas.
Adapt insights into original creative instead of copying competitor work.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to bypass access controls or private content.
Do not treat ad frequency as proof of performance without supporting data.
Do not copy competitor copy, images, layouts, or claims directly.

faq.question: Which ad libraries can this skill support?
faq.answer: It is written for public ad libraries such as Facebook Ad Library and LinkedIn ad sources.

faq.question: Does it guarantee performance data?
faq.answer: No. It can analyze visible patterns, but performance metrics depend on what the source exposes.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple competitors?
faq.answer: Yes. The prompts support multi-company comparisons across messages, audiences, formats, and campaign themes.

faq.question: Does it create final ad copy?
faq.answer: It can inform ad ideas, but users should write original copy for their brand and audience.

faq.question: Can it save screenshots and reports?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes saving screenshots, analysis reports, spreadsheet summaries, decks, and pattern libraries.

faq.question: Is it suitable for legal or compliance review?
faq.answer: No. Use legal guidance for platform terms, intellectual property questions, and regulated advertising claims.
